findings.title: Nil-SubType guard incomplete; vectorElemMinSize can nil-deref on nested SubType
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize recurses into vec.SubType without a nil check, so vectorFixedElemSize(nil) calls .Type() on a nil interface; a hand-built nested VectorType with 50 bytes and a *[][]float32 destination panics with a nil-pointer dereference.

findings.title: data != nil guard skips size bound for nil payload with huge Dimensions, untested
findings.claim: A nil payload with a huge Dimensions skips the bound intentionally since NULL is legal, but later code may still allocate from Dimensions for a nil payload (e.g. *any or *[N]T destination); this path was not traced and no test covers a large positive Dimensions with nil data.

findings.title: Unknown basic types now become CustomType instead of NativeType, with no test coverage
findings.claim: Every unknown basic type inside collections, tuples, UDTs and vectors now becomes CustomType with custom = name instead of a NativeType with empty custom string, changing String() and Custom() output; only the vector path is tested, nothing covers getCassandraLongType directly or unknown types nested in list, map or UDT, and the PR description doesn't mention this side effect.

findings.title: Saturation branch for overflowing minimum size is untested
findings.claim: math.MaxInt32 is returned when an inner vector's minimum size overflows; manual probing showed it works but TestVectorElemMinSize has no deeply nested or huge-dimension row covering this.

findings.title: PR description contains a Claude Code attribution line
findings.claim: The PR description contains a "🤖 Generated with Claude Code" line, which breaks the rule against attribution in PR bodies and should be removed.

findings.title: Allocation test relies on fragile process-wide TotalAlloc threshold
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating asserts on process-wide TotalAlloc with a payload/8 threshold; it is non-parallel but background goroutines from other packages' init or the runtime can still add allocations, so it could flake.
